name: Niagara Peninsula
terms: Vintners Quality Alliance, the appellation system for Canadian wine from British Columbia and Ontario. It guarantees the wine's origin.
Made from grapes frozen naturally on the vine and picked at 18°F (−8°C) or colder. Canada makes more than any other country, over 90% of it in Ontario.
keyfacts: The Niagara Peninsula has the largest planted area of any viticultural area in Canada, covering 13,600 acres.
It is bordered by Lake Ontario to the north, the Niagara River to the east, and the Welland River and Hamilton to the south and west.
The Niagara Escarpment, rising to some 575 feet above sea level, passes through the appellation, which holds 10 sub-appellations.
Ontario is one of the world's leading ice wine producers, and most of its ice wine is made from Riesling and Vidal.
Lake Ontario moderates air temperature, and the main grapes are Chardonnay, Riesling, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Franc.

notes: Ontario is the world's largest producer of icewine.
Ontario Chardonnay is often rich and oaky.
Ontario Cabernet Franc often shows a vegetal, raspberry-like flavor with moderate acidity.

blurb.text: A Canadian appellation that holds a dozen named areas, including Niagara-on-the-Lake, Niagara Escarpment, Beamsville Bench, Twenty Mile Bench and Short Hills Bench.
